title: Learning from First Discrepancies with Joint Reset and Pilot Guarantees
abstract: arXiv:2611.13913v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A run that stops at its first wrong decision shows the queries and their correct labels up to and including that decision, and nothing after it. We study how many such runs are needed for learning. Each run tests a hypothesis, the pilot, chosen beforehand from a fixed binary class of VC dimension at most $d$, on a fresh record of at most $D$ queries drawn from one unknown distribution that does not depend on the pilot. The terminal information of a record is shown only if the pilot makes no discrepancy, and a bounded loss, fixed in advance, is attached to the position where a hypothesis stops. If the discrepancy probabilities of members of the class have infimum at most $f$ and their risks have infimum at most $r$, one learner uses $\widetilde O((d+1)[D(f+\varepsilon)+r]/\varepsilon^2)$ runs and $\widetilde O(D(1+f/\varepsilon))$ distinct pilots on every history. It returns a member of the class and an interval of width at most $\varepsi

translated_title: 《基于首次分歧的学习：联合重置与先导假设保证》
translated_abstract: 一次在首个错误决策处停止的运行，会展示直到并包含该决策的查询及其正确标签，而此后的内容一概不可见。我们研究完成学习需要多少次这样的运行。每次运行在一 свеж新记录上测试一个事先从固定二元假设类（VC 维至多为 $d$）中选出的假设（称为“先导”），记录包含至多 $D$ 个查询，这些查询来自一个与先导无关的未知分布。只有当先导未产生任何分歧时，才展示记录的终止信息，并且一个事先固定的有界损失会附加在假设停止的位置上。若该类中成员的分歧概率的下确界至多为 $f$，且其风险的下确界至多为 $r$，则存在一个学习器，它在每个历史上使用 $\widetilde O((d+1)[D(f+\varepsilon)+r]/\varepsilon^2)$ 次运行和 $\widetilde O(D(1+f/\varepsilon))$ 个不同的先导。它返回该类中的一个成员以及一个宽度至多为 $\varepsilon$ 的区间。
tldr: 该论文研究了每次运行只揭示到首个错误决策为止信息的“首次分歧”学习模型，并证明当假设类（VC 维至多 $d$）的最优分歧概率至多为 $f$、最优风险至多为 $r$ 时，学习器仅需 $\widetilde O((d+1)[D(f+\varepsilon)+r]/\varepsilon^2)$ 次运行和 $\widetilde O(D(1+f/\varepsilon))$ 个先导假设，即可返回假设类成员及宽度至多 $\varepsilon$ 的风险区间，同时提供联合的重置与先导保证。
en_tdlr: This paper studies a "first discrepancy" learning model where each run reveals queries and correct labels only up to the first wrong decision, and proves that with $\widetilde O((d+1)[D(f+\varepsilon)+r]/\varepsilon^2)$ runs and $\widetilde O(D(1+f/\varepsilon)$ pilots, a learner can return a class member together with a risk interval of width at most $\varepsilon$, with joint reset and pilot guarantees.
